correctness.rationale: For δ=s+b−1≠0 the two affine branches share fixed center q=sb/δ outside [0,1]; logarithmic coordinate h(x)=log|x−q|/|q| divided by L conjugates the associated endpoint-identified circle map to rotation by ρ=log((1−s)/b)/L. The δ=0 case is the ordinary rotation x↦x+s. The invariant phase-uniform measure is normalized, with density 1/(|L||x−q|). The coordinate has exact Fourier coefficient 1/(L−2πik), so Parseval and the periodic Green kernel produce the claimed hyperbolic-cosine covariance, including the L=0 Bernoulli-polynomial limit. The branch bit is a rotation coding of [1−ρ,1); interval overlap yields covariance (ρ−t)_++(ρ+t−1)_+−ρ² and at t=ρ reaches −min(ρ,1−ρ)², the universal Fréchet lower bound. Mechanical-word telescoping proves discrepancy <1 and Sturmian N+1 factor complexity for irrational ρ. Rational rotations have other invariant measures; all statements correctly restrict to the specified Haar-pullback μ. Independent numerical quadrature across δ positive, negative and zero and lags 0,1,2,7 agrees with both analytic kernels.
